description:
Episode 23 of a daily journey through the universe. 💥
We go back to the Big Bang: 13.8 billion years ago, the first elements in three minutes, the cosmic dark ages, the first stars, and why your water is billions of years old.

segments.text: Episode twenty-three. Next stop... the Big Bang.
Thirteen point eight billion years ago, the universe began. Not as an explosion in space, but as space itself expanding.
segments.headline: 13.8 billion years ago

segments.text: Within its first three minutes, the first atomic nuclei formed, mostly hydrogen and helium.
For millions of years after, there were no stars at all. Astronomers call it the cosmic dark ages.
segments.headline: The cosmic dark ages

segments.text: The first stars switched on within roughly two hundred million years, lighting up the universe.
And the hydrogen in the water you drink was made in those first minutes.
segments.headline: Your water is 13.8 billion years old

segments.text: Tomorrow, we see the oldest galaxy ever found. Next stop: the edge of time, with the James Webb Telescope. Follow, so you don't miss episode twenty-four.
